subject: Deployment mode & HIPAA/BAA qualification - Acme Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode & HIPAA/BAA qualification - Acme Health

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to meet you both on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- Workload: PHI-containing clinical notes and patient messaging (low single-digit qps, bursty during business hours).
- Compliance: HIPAA required; customer legal requests a signed BAA. Also asked for SOC 2 Type II report and evidence of audit controls.
- Deployment preference: want to understand tradeoffs between Hosted API + BAA, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem (for audit isolation).

Redwood recommendation (initial):
1) Start with Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable throughput and data isolation while you finalize procurement, this gives isolation and SLA without immediate on-prem work.
2) Parallel: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a standard BAA for legal review. If you need full VPC/on-prem for contractual/audit reasons we can scope that as a next-phase private deployment.

Next steps I propose:
- I will share our SOC 2 report and a BAA draft (attached). Rishi will follow up with architecture options and an implementation checklist for Dedicated and Private VPC.
- Can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra/security team this week or early next? Suggest Thurs 09/24 or Mon 09/28.
- Please send any specific audit items or evidentiary requests (e.g., access logs, retention policy, key management) you want us to include in the follow-up packet.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_v3.pdf (SOC 2 Type II redacted), BAA_Draft_Acme_20260921.docx (editable)

Thanks again, happy to sync whenever works.

Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[d] +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA/BAA qualification - Acme Health

Dylan,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Volume: correct on low qps but we do have around a 10x burst during nightly triage windows. Latency targets are 200-300ms p50 for user-facing flows.
- SOC 2: our security team will want to review the Type II report and the controls matrix. Can you confirm whether you provide evidence for encryption-at-rest KMS usage and key rotation policy?
- BAA: we prefer to run your draft through our legal. We may redline the BAA to require on-site audit rights for a third party, would that block a Dedicated deployment?

We can do Thurs 09/24 at 11am ET for the technical deep-dive, that works for Priya and me. Please send a calendar invite and include Rishi / your security engineering lead.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of IT Security | Acme Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA/BAA qualification - Acme Health

Alex / team,

Thanks, I'll own the technical packet for the deep-dive on 09/24 11am ET and follow up here with a short architecture summary and answers to your SOC 2 questions before the call. Preliminary answers below: 

Quick answers to the SOC 2 / KMS questions:
- Encryption at rest: yes, all customer data at rest is encrypted. For Hosted and Dedicated we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private VPC (we can support AWS KMS and GCP KMS).
- Key rotation: keys are rotated per our KMS provider policies; we can provide rotation proof and key lifecycle documentation as part of the evidence packet.
- On-site audit rights: a Dedicated deployment (customer-dedicated GPU pool) doesn't by itself prevent a contractual right to an on-site audit, but operationally most customers use a combination of auditor access to logs, retained evidence, and third-party attestations (SOC 2) instead of physical on-site inspections. If your legal requires physical on-site audits we can scope Private/on-prem as an option, I'll ask Hannah (legal) to confirm what we can accommodate contractually.

Attached for pre-read: Redwood_SOC2_Report_v3.pdf (redacted controls matrix), Dedicated_vs_Private_implementation_checklist.pdf (short checklist).

Agenda for 09/24 deep-dive (30 min):
- 5m: introductions + goals
- 10m: architecture options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - tradeoffs for HIPAA workloads
- 10m: evidence & timelines (SOC 2 items, BAA turnaround, audit evidence)
- 5m: next steps / procurement path (PO / contract owner)

Action items we'll cover before the call:
- Dylan: send calendar invite + HubSpot deal owners / procurement contacts.
- Alex/Priya: send any required evidentiary checklist you have (e.g., specific Audit IDs).

Thanks, looking forward to the call.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & HIPAA/BAA qualification - Acme Health

Dylan / Rishi,

Thanks, invite received for Thu 11am ET. Priya will share our audit checklist ahead of the meeting (expected by EOD today). Two quick asks we want included in the pre-read: 
- Sample logging retention policy (30/90/365 day options) and how logs are exported for third-party auditors.
- Confirm whether Dedicated includes network isolation (VPC peering or private link) by default or needs extra configuration.

If all looks good we'll aim to pilot on Dedicated for 1-2 months and then evaluate whether to move to Private VPC for long-term contractual audit requirements.

Alex
